_meta.note: Two improvements from an external (Codex) retrospective, both deepening HeartBeat's real differentiator — an EVIDENCE LIFECYCLE (a task result is provisional until executable evidence AND an attempted refutation agree). (LC) Today the gate-pass snapshot commits+TAGS GATE_x on the DETERMINISTIC pass (gate.sh:139 / gate.py:69), before the adversarial review — so for a review-gated phase the tag briefly certifies an un-reviewed / later-refuted state, and a refute→fix cycle churns the tag and doubles the checkpoint. Fix: for a gate WITH a `review` block, defer the commit+tag to REVIEW ACCEPTANCE (`hb review <gate> pass`); non-review gates snapshot at the deterministic pass, unchanged. Invariant: `git reset --hard GATE_x` always restores a state that passed BOTH the deterministic gate and the review. (RQ) Method quality depends on the reviewer prompt. Generate falsification questions from the gate's own claims: extend hb-audit with a `--questions <gate>` mode that, per criterion, classifies it (reusing the existing vacuous/existence/behavioral taxonomy + grep-of-source / coverage-grep / side-effect detection) and emits a targeted 'how could this FALSELY pass?' question, plus a general phase question — seeding the refuter deterministically. Both are CORE (domain-agnostic) + a PARITY surface (node ≡ python). Proof-driven: spec-first, gated, refuted.

phases.title: Checkpoint lifecycle — tag only on reviewed acceptance

tasks.title: Spec-first: proof for the deferred-tag lifecycle
tasks.description: Author RED-first. docs/howto/gate-examples/gate-review-checkpoint.sh (prints CHECKPOINT-LIFECYCLE-OK): in a throwaway git project bootstrapped with `plugin/bootstrap.sh`, write a dag.json with (a) a REVIEW-GATED gate and (b) a NON-review gate, each with one trivially-passing criterion. Assert: running `.hb/gate.sh <review-gate>` reports review_pending and creates NO `<review-gate>` git tag yet; then `node .hb/hb.js review <review-gate> pass --artifact <file>` (artifact >40 chars, HB_ACTOR distinct) creates the tag on HEAD. Assert the NON-review gate DOES get its tag at deterministic pass (unchanged). Then repeat the review-gate scenario via the PYTHON runtime (`python3 -m heartbeat.cli init` + `hb gate` + `hb review … pass`) and assert the SAME tag-timing (node ≡ python). Must FAIL now (current code tags at the deterministic pass) — confirm red.

tasks.title: Defer the snapshot to review acceptance (both runtimes)
tasks.description: plugin/templates/gate.sh: when the passing gate HAS a `review` block, do NOT call git_snapshot at the deterministic pass (skip commit+tag); a gate with no review snapshots as today. py/src/heartbeat/gate.py: same guard around `_git_snapshot` (skip when the gate has a review). Then create the snapshot at REVIEW ACCEPTANCE: in plugin/templates/hb.js's review command (case 'review' → verdict pass), after recording `review_passed`, commit the working tree and force-tag the gate (a git-snapshot mirroring gate.sh's git_snapshot, honoring HB_NO_GIT / HB_GIT_AUTOCOMMIT); in py/src/heartbeat/cli.py's review-pass path (after the review_passed event) call `gate._git_snapshot(hb, gate)`. Keep node ≡ python behavior. Make gate-review-checkpoint.sh pass.

phases.title: Generate adversarial review questions from the gate's claims

tasks.title: Spec-first: proof + fixture for the question generator
tasks.description: Author RED-first. Fixture plugin/templates/fixtures/questions.dag.json (this exact path — the gate criteria pin it) with a gate named exactly GATE_P0 whose criteria span classes: an existence check (`test -f …`), a grep-of-source (`grep -q 'def foo' src.py`), a coverage-grep (`… | grep -q Tnn`), and a real behavioral (`python3 -c 'import m; assert m.foo()==2'`). Proof docs/howto/gate-examples/review-questions.sh (prints REVIEW-QUESTIONS-OK): `node plugin/templates/hb-audit.js <fixture> --questions <gate>` emits, PER criterion, a falsification question keyed to its class (existence → 'presence ≠ behavior'; grep-source → 'could pass on a hollow stub — is the code executed?'; coverage-grep → 'does it assert the group PASSED, not just a printed header?'; behavioral → 'does it pin the REAL required behavior or a weak proxy?') PLUS one general phase question referencing the gate `desc` ('how could every criterion pass while the feature is still broken?'). Assert each class's question is present and node ≡ python byte-identical (`python3 -m heartbeat.cli audit --questions <gate> --dir <proj>` or the audit module). Must FAIL now (no --questions mode) — confirm red.

Mirror it in py/src/heartbeat/audit.py (a `review_questions(dag, gate)` function) exposed via the CLI (`hb audit --questions <gate>`), BYTE-IDENTICAL output to node.
